title: Taking Each Other in Our Arms
text:
Taking each other in our arms,

each giving oneself to the other's arms.

How different to feel you inside one

than to feel oneself alone inside one

that is, empty.

Could your embrace be loneliness

and your kisses only thirst?

I seem to hear you saying you are never sated with me.

I who before was a good taster of bitterness.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's movement from embrace to loneliness and its final self-recognition.

title: The Sweetness of Certain Words Such As
text:
The sweetness of certain words such as

'us two.'

I wander solitary among kisses.

From my solitudes I come

may I not return to my solitudes.

I felt that eternity

will be the two of us together.

God who loves me as if I were God.

Someday I will be an expert in loves

in your bed, between the sheets.

Sex of God.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's mingling of erotic and divine intimacy, including its abrupt closing phrase.

title: Epigram I
text:
But at night

you have your rice

and your fried beans,

with fresh

curds,

and a hot tortilla,

or a roasted plantain,

you eat it without bodyguards

and your sad

gourd-cup

is not tasted

first by an aide.

And afterward you play

if you want on

your guitar

a ranchera

song,

and you do not sleep

surrounded by searchlights

and barbed wire
editorial_note: The translation keeps the humble meal and music as freedom from the guarded life of power.

title: Epitaph for the Tomb of Adolfo Báez Bone
text:
They killed you and did not

tell us where

they buried your body,

but since then

the whole territory

is your sepulcher

or rather:

in every span

of national territory

where

your body is not

you resurrected

they believed they were

killing you with an order

of Fire!

they believed they were

burying you

and what they were doing

was burying a seed.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the epitaph's transformation of a hidden body into national resurrection.

title: From These Movie Theaters, Claudia, These Parties
text:
From these movie theaters, Claudia, these parties,

these horse races,

nothing will remain for posterity

except Ernesto Cardenal's verses for Claudia

(if at all)

and Claudia's name that I put in those verses

and those of my rivals, if I decide to rescue them

from oblivion, and include them too in my

verses

to ridicule them.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the mock-grand claim that poems may preserve Claudia and even the rivals they mock.
